title: P99 SSO WebSocket Protocol
description: Normative machine-readable wire contract for the WebSocket channel between the P99 login proxy (client) and an SSO backend (reference implementation: roboToald). Owned by and kept only in the p99-login-proxy repo. Each message is a JSON object discriminated by its `type`. Bulk payloads (account_tree, changes) are loosely typed so the server can evolve their internals without breaking clients; unknown extra fields are permitted everywhere for the same reason. For flows, crypto, RBAC, size caps, and implementer checklists see docs/backend-protocol.md in p99-login-proxy (additive guide; must not diverge from this schema).

full_state.description: Server -> client. Full snapshot of the accessible account tree. Working server and proxy always exchange account_tree, count, and dynamic tag lists.

login_auth_response.description: Server -> client. Result of a login_auth request, matched by the echoed `request_id`. On success `real_user` and `encrypted_credentials` (Base64 DES-CBC) are present, plus `notes` when the server-resolved account or any of its characters has login notes; on failure `error` (and `status`: 400, 401, 410 or 500) are present.

login_notes.description: Login notes for the account that login_auth resolved to (tags resolve server-side). Omitted when there are none. Plain text (at most 500 characters each in the reference server); clients must not interpret it as markup.

characters.description: Character name -> notes, only for characters of the resolved account that have notes.

ping.description: Keepalive. Either direction (server typically sends; client may also send).

error.description: Server -> client. Terminal error / auth rejection. Working server always sets `detail`; proxy UI reads `detail` only. `message` / `reason` are optional aliases.

show_modal.description: Server -> client. Generic popup, independent of any request. Plain text; clients must not interpret it as markup. Clients route it through the same popup handling as their built-in popups (login notes, rejected logins, connection errors). Older clients ignore it.

id.description: Optional. A popup whose id matches one the client still has pending is dropped.

level.description: Icon and styling. Default info; clients treat unknown values as info.

always_on_top.description: Show in a separate window that stays above other windows until acknowledged, instead of a dialog in the proxy window. Default false.

auth.description: Client -> server. First message after connect; authenticates the session. `client_settings` carries `log_enabled` and, once checked, `rustle_present` (booleans) for guild policy checks.

login_auth.description: Client -> server. Request real credentials for an alias/tag.

heartbeat.description: Client -> server. Periodic liveness for a logged-in character.

update_location.description: Client -> server. Character park/bind/level/item updates. Locations are zone keys. All fields besides character_name are optional; `items` is a partial update of the item wire keys. Legacy clients may send `keys`; server merges with `items` (`items` wins on conflict).

update_inventory.description: Client -> server. Raw EQ `<Char>-Inventory.txt` export (`/outputfile inventory`). The server parses tracked items from it and treats the result as a full snapshot of the tracked item columns. Blank text, text longer than 524288 bytes, or text with no `Name` column is ignored.

update_spellbook.description: Client -> server. Raw EQ `<Char>-Spellbook.txt` export (`/outputfile spellbook`): one `<level><TAB><spell name>` line per scribed spell, unsorted, no header (spaces are accepted in place of the tab). The server replaces the character's stored spellbook with it. Store only: spells never appear in full_state or delta. Blank text, text longer than 131072 bytes, any non-blank line that is not a level (1-255) and a name, a name longer than 255 characters, or more than 1000 distinct spells is ignored.

fte.description: Client -> server. First-to-engage report for a raid mob.

mob_death.description: Client -> server. Raid mob death report.

faction_hits.description: Client -> server. Faction-standing lines one character logged within one EQ log second: `Your faction standing with <faction> got better|worse.` (`better` / `worse`) and `... could not possibly get any better|worse.` (`max` / `min`, the faction is capped). `faction` is the log text verbatim. Store only: never appears in full_state or delta. The server reads at most the first 50 hits and skips entries whose trimmed `faction` is empty or longer than 255 characters.
